extracted.intended_audience: creative nonfiction writers and writing students (memoir/flash nonfiction)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and exemplar-based advice for writing and teaching concise literary nonfiction (flash essays and memoir), with emphasis on sentence-level craft, openings, use of form, and revision for brevity. The page collects favorite Brevity pieces as models and extracts craft lessons from them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concision / brevity
rubrics_metrics.description: Brevity: A Journal of Concise Literary Nonfiction; pieces are short and demand economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shorten drafts; trim adjectives and adverbs; 'shoot the darlings' and 'hack out the boring parts.' Almost every draft will be improved by shortening it. Use Brevity pieces as models for tight, economical writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence-level quality ('Every sentence must be good')
rubrics_metrics.description: Not Every Sentence Can Be Great But Every Sentence Must Be Good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate sentences individually (example exercise: pick a random novel page and judge the first sentence). Move sentences from boring to good through revision; aim for consistently serviceable, well-crafted sentences throughout a piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restraint in language ('write cool when the action is hot')
rubrics_metrics.description: In scenes with strong feelings writers often want to match them with forceful language; instead, 'write cool when the action is hot.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pull back language to increase emotion in the reader — restraint can intensify feeling rather than weaken it. Study essays (e.g., on the Earley Scale, Edwidge Danticat) that model cooler diction during hot moments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powerful opening / start close to the action ('smoke jumper' metaphor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dinty Moore describes the reader as a 'smoke jumper' who lands close to the fire; words must be hot from the first sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin near the emotional/core image or event (in medias res). Your opening should land the reader immediately in the scene or emotional center — make the first sentence 'hot' and immediately compelling (examples: 'The Water is Rising Pleas').

rubrics_metrics.name: Use images, headlines, and photographs as prompts
rubrics_metrics.description: Use images (photos/video) or headlines as inspiration or structural material for an essay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write from photographs (imagine narrators/subjects in photos), or craft pieces inspired by headlines and visual stimuli. Examples include 'On the Farm' (writing from photos) and essays modeled on images/headlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: List-making as a structural device and prompt
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists can be a productive form for short nonfiction; many works are crafted from lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If stuck, make a list (e.g., mundane objects within five feet) and use it as impetus for an essay or poem. Lists can generate structure, images, and unexpected connections (example: 'Things That Appear Ugly Or Troubling But Upon Closer Inspection Are Beautiful').

rubrics_metrics.name: Form choice (use of epistolary and other flash forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliberate formal choices — such as epistolary structure — can shape flash nonfiction and produce effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study pieces (e.g., 'Swerve') that use epistolary form or other constrained formats as models. Consider form as a tool to deliver voice, surprise, or compression; read companion pieces about why the form was chosen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unexamined slant / demand for narrative clarity and craft
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers may unconsciously 'lay out facts in a row and slant them towards their own hurt feelings'; adult reflection brings clarity and the need to craft rather than merely vent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure memoir/essay moves beyond airing grievance — present reflection, context, and craft. If a piece simply arranges facts to justify an emotional claim, it may not 'work'; strive for honest, examined perspective and craft-based shaping of material.
